newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Feuding Nigerian oil tribes appeal to military.
newsitem.headline: Feuding Nigerian oil tribes appeal to military.

text.p: Feuding tribes in Nigeria's oil-producing Warri area on Thursday traded accusations of murder and arson and called separately on the military for help.
Hostilities started on March 22 when clashes between armed youths broke out over a move of the local council headquarters from an Ijaw town to that of the rival Itsekiri tribe.
In an appeal to military strongman General Sani Abacha, the Itsekiri chiefs called for a tribunal to resolve the fighting which has hit oil production by Royal Dutch Shell.
"The Ijaw have not relented in wreaking violence on the Itsekiri. What have they done? Pogrom, mayhem, arson and ethnic cleansing," the statement said.
But a group calling itself "Concerned Ijaw Citizens" produced a counter-charge that Iteskiris had bribed members of the security forces "to attack and kill Ijaws".
Newspapers quoted a prominent Itsekiri chief, D.O. Odegbe, as saying that over 1,000 of his kinsmen had been killed in the fighting and 3,000 wounded.
But independent figures are hard to come by in the tangle of creeks and swamps where the clashes are going on, and news reports have only spoken of dozens of dead.
The Guardian newspaper on Thursday said military forces were heading from Warri into the hinterland to quell the disturbances by boat and helicopter.

Shell said last week it could not meet contracts for the supply of some 80,000 barrels per day of crude oil from the area, but is working to reopen flow stations closed by the disturbances and restore production.
